clue.text: Informant poking around without gain in mind

indicators.note: poking around suggests rummaging and stirring things up, so the letters are moved about into a new order

parts.note: the fifteen letters of these two words are the raw material

explanation.surface: A police informer nosing about who is not doing it for money.
explanation.definitionFit: A non-profit-making body operates with no aim of earning a surplus, so it acts with no gain intended.

clue.text: My turn to listen? That's more like it

definitions.meaning: first meaning, read literally: the other person is speaking at last, so I get to hear them
second meaning: the idiom of approval when someone finally says something welcome

explanation.walkthrough: The literal reading of the phrase gives the first half; the everyday idiom of approval gives the second.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom expresses approval of a better offer or suggestion, while literally it marks the other party starting to speak.

indicators.note: a word unaware of something lacks it, so that letter is taken away

parts.note: a native is a born citizen of a place
T is the standard abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A sheltered resident who has no idea what time it is.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone naive lacks experience of the world, which is exactly being unworldly or innocent.

clue.text: He's finished his work about Hebridean island

parts.note: re is Latin-derived for concerning or about
Tiree is one of the Inner Hebrides off western Scotland

explanation.surface: A man who has completed some piece of writing on a Scottish island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Finished his work' reads as completing a book; the definition means finished working for good.
explanation.definitionFit: A retiree has stopped employment for good, so his working life is over.

clue.text: Boasts loud and long to relatives

parts.note: f, forte, is the musical marking for loud
L is the abbreviation for long
aunts are family relatives

explanation.surface: Someone bragging noisily and at length to their family.
explanation.definitionFit: To flaunt is to show off, so the verb in the third person is a synonym of boasts.

clue.text: Funny foreign article seen in backstreet strolls

indicators.note: things seen in a place sit inside it, so these pieces go inside the other
back attached to the street tells us to read that word from the end

parts.note: the street part is St, the abbreviation for street; back is the instruction
funny in the sense of strange or peculiar
le is the French definite article

explanation.surface: A strange foreign newspaper piece found in a side street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backstreet' looks like one word for an alley but splits into an instruction and a street abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: To toddle is to walk in an unhurried, ambling way, a near synonym of stroll.

clue.text: Old-fashioned complex equation leaving nothing out

indicators.note: complex means intricate or tangled, so the letters are mixed into another order
leaving with out means omitting, so one letter is dropped from the word

parts.note: taken as written
nothing is zero, which looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: A maths sum that is outdated and complicated yet leaves nothing out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaving nothing out' sounds like thoroughness; it instructs us to remove the zero-shaped letter before rearranging.
explanation.definitionFit: Antique describes something from an earlier era, which is what old-fashioned means.

indicators.note: in a down answer, what comes beneath follows the earlier piece
hearing tells us the words are judged by how they sound when spoken

parts.note: an inn is a pub
a spectre is a ghost

explanation.surface: A detective listening for a phantom in the cellar of a pub.
explanation.definitionFit: An inspector is a police rank above sergeant, so the word names a policeman.

indicators.note: something suffering is in a bad state and disordered, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: the fifteen letters of both words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A patient whose stubborn thyroid swelling has become infected.
explanation.definitionFit: Gastroenteritis is inflammation of stomach and intestines, usually caused by a viral or bacterial infection.

clue.text: Conservationist's maxim, we hear, finishes off a lot of clothing

definitions.text: finishes off a lot of clothing
definitions.note: a descriptive clause: the band that finishes off many garments

indicators.note: we hear means the phrase is said out loud and spelt differently

parts.note: a green motto forbidding wastefulness

explanation.surface: An environmental slogan that apparently ruins most of one's outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a description rather than a synonym: skirts and trousers are finished at the top by this strip.
explanation.definitionFit: A waistband is the strip of fabric forming the top edge of trousers or skirts, finishing the garment.

parts.note: surface reading: a brass player's prominent front teeth
setter's reading: the trumpeter is an elephant, famous for trumpeting, and these are its ivory teeth

explanation.walkthrough: A trumpeter here is not a musician but the animal that trumpets.
explanation.definitionFit: Elephants trumpet, and their long ivory incisors are the big teeth meant.

clue.text: Two elements of cricket go on for too long

parts.note: first element: an over is a set of six balls bowled in cricket
second element: a run is the basic unit of scoring in cricket

explanation.surface: A cricket match that drags on past its scheduled time.
explanation.walkthrough: Over and run are both standard cricket terms.
explanation.definitionFit: To overrun is to exceed an allotted time, i.e. continue longer than planned.

clue.text: Retained by both sides, I line up endless drink

indicators.note: something retained by another is held inside it, so these go between

parts.note: left and right, the two sides

indicators.note: endless means without its last letter, so the final one goes

parts.note: taken as written
to queue is to line up

explanation.surface: Someone queuing endlessly for a drink while held by both arms.
explanation.definitionFit: A liqueur is a sweet, flavoured spirit, a kind of alcoholic drink.

indicators.note: regularly means at fixed intervals, so every other letter is taken

parts.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters

explanation.surface: An instruction to caress a little limb now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: The published key shows TEE, but the wordplay and definition both point to TOE; the middle square has no crossing.
explanation.definitionFit: A toe is a digit of the foot, a small body part or member.

parts.note: a ram is a male sheep
jets is to fly by jet

explanation.surface: A farmer's way of herding sheep, with insects buzzing around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flies' looks like a noun for insects; it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A ramjet is a type of jet engine, a mechanism that propels an aircraft.

parts.note: mares are female horses, so female beasts
a tail is at the rear

explanation.surface: Nasty women raising a weed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beastly' suggests unpleasant, but means belonging to beasts.
explanation.definitionFit: Mare's-tail is a persistent garden weed, so a plant gardeners do not want.

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a slang word for a woman's breast

explanation.walkthrough: The possessive makes the clue look like a bird's chest; the 's is just 'is' joining two meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a small garden songbird and, in vulgar slang, a female breast.

indicators.note: unconventional means not in the usual way, so the letters are set in a different order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Honouring an unusual emblem of power.
explanation.definitionFit: A sceptre is a ceremonial staff carried by a monarch to represent sovereign power.

indicators.note: without means lacking, so that piece is removed

parts.note: to coax is to persuade or tempt

indicators.note: half of a two-letter word is just one of its letters

parts.note: the first of the two letters

explanation.surface: Eve's temptation in Eden, with only half an apple.
explanation.walkthrough: Cox's Orange Pippin is a well-known English apple variety, usually called a Cox.
explanation.definitionFit: A Cox is a popular variety of English eating apple.

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one word goes round the other

parts.note: to treat with someone is to negotiate
H is the map symbol for hospital

explanation.surface: Bargaining over hospital dangers.
explanation.definitionFit: Threats are things likely to cause harm, so they are dangers or risks.

explanation.walkthrough: The question reads as worry about a medicine's safety; the word is both the medicine and the quality asked about.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a noun for a pain-relieving medicine and an adjective for something inoffensive.

clue.text: Reckoned shillings for pence, being led astray

indicators.note: for here means in place of, so one letter swaps in for another

parts.note: deduced means worked out or reckoned
s was the abbreviation for the old British shilling
d was the abbreviation for the old British penny

explanation.surface: Someone working out old British money while being tricked.
explanation.walkthrough: In pre-decimal British currency, shillings were 's' and pence 'd' (from Latin denarius); the first D swaps for S.
explanation.definitionFit: To be seduced is to be enticed or tempted into wrongdoing, i.e. led astray.

indicators.note: one letter placed in a word sits inside it

parts.note: bar as a preposition means except
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A correct route into a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Passage' reads as a corridor and 'bar' as a pub, but bar means except.
explanation.definitionFit: An excerpt is a short extract from a text, also called a passage.

clue.text: Involve little brother in climbing tree

indicators.note: in puts one piece inside the other
in a down clue climbing means going upwards, so the word reads bottom to top

parts.note: the lime, or linden, is a tree
bro is a short form of brother

explanation.surface: Getting a younger sibling involved when he climbs a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: To embroil is to drag someone into a conflict or situation, i.e. involve them.

clue.text: Is competitor initially below form for big race?

indicators.note: in a down clue below means placed after the other piece

parts.note: a form is a school class

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so each word gives only its opening letter

parts.note: the first letters of both words

explanation.surface: Asking whether a runner's past form makes them a contender in a major race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Form' suggests a horse's past results but means a school year group. The Classics are five major British flat horse races, such as the Derby.
explanation.definitionFit: A classic is one of the five chief annual flat races in British horse racing.

indicators.note: used in says the letters are found inside the following word

parts.note: the middle three letters

explanation.surface: Timber employed to make a curtain pelmet.
explanation.walkthrough: A pelmet is a board or frame above a window that hides the curtain rail.
explanation.definitionFit: Elm is a hardwood tree, and its timber is called elm too.

clue.text: Girl with dictionary tied up with string?

parts.note: lass is a girl
OED is the Oxford English Dictionary

explanation.surface: A girl with a dictionary bound up with cord.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that a lasso is rope rather than string, a playful stretch.
explanation.definitionFit: Lassoed means caught with a looped rope, a heavier version of being tied with cord.

clue.text: Old transporter working less, without initial fire

indicators.note: without its initial means the opening letter is dropped

parts.note: BR is British Rail, the former national railway
lazier means doing less work

explanation.surface: An old lorry or carrier doing less work, with nothing to light it.
explanation.walkthrough: British Rail ran Britain's trains until privatisation in the 1990s, so it is an old transporter.
explanation.definitionFit: A brazier is a metal container holding burning coals, an outdoor fire.

indicators.note: almost means not quite complete, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: an image is a picture
O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: A near-photographic image of an ancient bug.
explanation.definitionFit: An imago is the final, adult stage of an insect after metamorphosis.

clue.text: Indexer's first list left out country

indicators.note: first picks the opening letter of the word before it

parts.note: the opening letter

indicators.note: out means removed, so that letter goes

parts.note: a tally is a running list or count
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A book indexer omitting a nation from their first list.
explanation.definitionFit: Italy is a European country.

indicators.note: something that eats takes it inside, so one piece is swallowed by the other

parts.note: cross means annoyed or angry
I is the Roman numeral one
the worker ant is the crossword's standard worker

explanation.surface: A cross employee eating a bread roll.
explanation.definitionFit: A croissant is a crescent-shaped bread roll made of flaky pastry.

parts.note: golden as in a golden opportunity, full of promise
good to eat, i.e. delicious

explanation.surface: Fruit that looks promising and tastes good.
explanation.definitionFit: Golden Delicious is a popular yellow-skinned apple variety, a fruit.
